leading/hy_oas.title: High-yield credit spread (OAS)
leading/hy_oas.why: Credit spreads typically widen before equity drawdowns deepen and tighten before durable equity bottoms; this is the confirmation channel for any equity stress. The same series is carried by the Market Pulse layer; it is archived here as well because the fingerprint states are computed only from this section's own archive.
leading/hy_oas.definition: ICE BofA US High Yield Index option-adjusted spread (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2); daily, in percent.
leading/hy_oas.note: Widely used as the credit-confirmation gauge: the fingerprint bar is +0.50 of widening over 21 sessions.

leading/ig_oas.title: Investment-grade credit spread (OAS)
leading/ig_oas.why: Slower, higher-quality credit. IG widening after HY-only widening marks stress graduating up the quality ladder; IG staying calm while HY widens marks a contained, low-quality event.
leading/ig_oas.definition: ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread (FRED BAMLC0A0CM); daily, in percent.

leading/ebp.title: Excess bond premium
leading/ebp.why: The Gilchrist–Zakrajšek credit-sentiment component of corporate spreads: the part of spreads not explained by expected default. It rises ahead of recessions and equity bear markets in the Fed's own work, and led the 2007–08 widening. Read by the existing pulse fetcher from the same FEDS Notes file.
leading/ebp.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Notes EBP series — federalreserve.gov
leading/ebp.definition: Excess Bond Premium (Gilchrist–Zakrajšek methodology, FEDS Notes series) — the non-default component of corporate bond spreads; monthly, in percentage points.
leading/ebp.note: Monthly and revised with the FEDS vintage; a sentiment gauge, not a traded price.

leading/nfci.title: Chicago Fed NFCI
leading/nfci.why: Composite financial conditions lead real activity and risk-asset stress by construction of the Chicago Fed's factor model (105 weekly series). Positive = tighter than average. The level is the section's conditions anchor: markets can fall a long way while this still prints loose, and that gap is a classification signal.
leading/nfci.definition: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index (FRED NFCI); weekly (week ended Wednesday, published Friday), index (0 = average conditions).
leading/nfci.note: Restated by the Chicago Fed as source data revise; the archive keeps the latest vintage.

leading/nfci_credit.title: NFCI — credit subindex
leading/nfci_credit.why: The credit component of the NFCI: credit reprices fast *during* events, so this subindex is the coincident-to-early read on whether a market move is becoming a funding problem.
leading/nfci_credit.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI credit subindex (FRED NFCICREDIT); weekly, index (0 = average).

leading/nfci_leverage.title: NFCI — leverage subindex
leading/nfci_leverage.why: The leverage component of the NFCI: leverage builds slowly *before* events, so a rising leverage subindex from a low base is the quiet vulnerability signal — the mirror image of the credit subindex's fast repricing.
leading/nfci_leverage.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI leverage subindex (FRED NFCILEVERAGE); weekly, index (0 = average).

leading/nfci_risk.title: NFCI — risk subindex
leading/nfci_risk.why: The risk component of the NFCI (volatility and risk-appetite measures): the fastest-moving of the three subindexes, and the one that should move first if a vol event is becoming a conditions event.
leading/nfci_risk.definition: Chicago Fed NFCI risk subindex (FRED NFCIRISK); weekly, index (0 = average).

leading/anfci.title: Chicago Fed ANFCI (adjusted)
leading/anfci.why: The NFCI adjusted to remove the part of conditions explained by the state of the economy itself — the purer financial impulse. Agreement between NFCI and ANFCI is a robustness check on the conditions read.
leading/anfci.definition: Chicago Fed Adjusted NFCI (FRED ANFCI); weekly, index (0 = average conditions).

leading/stlfsi4.title: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
leading/stlfsi4.why: A second conditions composite, built differently (18 weekly rates, spreads and vol series, principal components). Agreement between STLFSI4 and the NFCI family is the robustness check; divergence is itself information about which construction is driving the read.
leading/stlfsi4.definition: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index, version 4 (FRED STLFSI4); weekly, index (0 = average stress).

leading/vix.title: VIX (spot)
leading/vix.why: The 30-day implied volatility of the S&P 500. Spot vol is coincident, but its level against the 3-month VIX (the derived spread below) is one of the cleanest stress fingerprints in free data.
leading/vix.definition: CBOE Volatility Index, daily close (FRED VIXCLS); daily, in vol points.

leading/vxv.title: VIX 3-month (VXV)
leading/vxv.why: The 3-month implied volatility of the S&P 500 — the denominator of the vol term structure. Spot above 3-month (backwardation) marks dislocation onset; normalisation has historically been among the earliest signs a dislocation is ending.
leading/vxv.definition: CBOE VIX 3-Month Volatility Index, daily close (FRED VXVCLS); daily, in vol points.

leading/gvz.title: Gold vol (GVZ)
leading/gvz.why: Implied volatility of gold. A companion to the equity vol panel: gold vol rising with equity vol marks a broad haven scramble; gold vol calm while equity vol spikes marks an equity-local event.
leading/gvz.definition: CBOE Gold ETF Volatility Index, daily close (FRED GVZCLS); daily, in vol points.

leading/ovx.title: Oil vol (OVX)
leading/ovx.why: Implied volatility of crude oil. The companion gauge for energy shocks: an oil price move with OVX spiking is a supply-scare signature; the same move with OVX falling is an unwind.
leading/ovx.definition: CBOE Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index, daily close (FRED OVXCLS); daily, in vol points.

leading/t10y2y.title: Yield curve, 10y − 2y
leading/t10y2y.why: The classic slow lead: inversion precedes recessions by quarters. The nearer-term signal this series contributes is the inflection — re-steepening after inversion has historically sat much closer to recessions than the inversion itself (Section 4 of the methodology).
leading/t10y2y.definition: 10-year Treasury yield minus 2-year Treasury yield (FRED T10Y2Y); daily, in percentage points.

leading/t10y3m.title: Yield curve, 10y − 3m
leading/t10y3m.why: The 10y−3m slope — the curve measure in the New York Fed's recession-probability model. Shown beside 10y−2y because the two can disagree when the front end is pinned by the expected policy path.
leading/t10y3m.definition: 10-year Treasury yield minus 3-month Treasury yield (FRED T10Y3M); daily, in percentage points.

leading/claims.title: Initial jobless claims
leading/claims.why: The fastest hard-data labour series (weekly, one-week lag). A sustained turn up in claims is the standard early recession tell; claims staying low while markets fall is itself a classification signal — a financial event, not yet a macro event.
leading/claims.definition: Initial claims for unemployment insurance, seasonally adjusted (FRED ICSA); weekly, in persons.

leading/sentiment.title: Consumer sentiment (Michigan)
leading/sentiment.why: Household expectations turn early but noisily. Included as context and weighted accordingly: monthly, survey-based, and prone to partisan swings that do not map to spending.
leading/sentiment.definition: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment index (FRED UMCSENT); monthly, index (1966 = 100).
leading/sentiment.note: Labelled monthly and noisy on the page, per the design: context, not a trigger.

sectors/soxx.title: Semiconductors (SOXX)
sectors/soxx.why: Semiconductors are the highest-beta expression of the AI-capex complex and usually its most volatile panel; a grid member in their own right, not folded into technology.

sectors/kre.title: Regional banks (KRE)
sectors/kre.why: Regional banks are where equity stress becomes funding stress first (2023 is the template). A grid member because its quadrant is an early read on whether a selloff is reaching the banking system.
sectors/kre.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: KRE — finance.yahoo.com/quote/KRE

sectors/xhb.title: Homebuilders (XHB)

sectors/xhb.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: XHB (unadjusted close)

sectors/sphb.title: High beta (SPHB)
sectors/sphb.why: The risk-appetite leg of the factor pair. The SPHB−SPLV 60-session spread (the pulse layer's factor_rotation series, same construction) is the displayed cross-check on the rotation fingerprint: high beta rolling over before the index is the classic early tell.

sectors/sphb.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: SPHB (unadjusted close)
sectors/sphb.definition: Daily unadjusted close of Invesco S&P 500 High Beta ETF (SPHB), in USD; trading days only.

sectors/splv.title: Low volatility (SPLV)

crossasset/sp500.title: S&P 500 index
crossasset/sp500.why: The index level itself (FRED's daily S&P 500), shown beside the SPY ETF so index and traded price can be compared; the movers table's equity anchor.
crossasset/sp500.definition: S&P 500 index level (FRED SP500); daily, in index points.

crossasset/nasdaq.title: Nasdaq Composite
crossasset/nasdaq.why: The broader growth tape. Nasdaq's one-day snaps in a drawdown are the raw material the snapback state tests at the 5-session window.
crossasset/nasdaq.definition: Nasdaq Composite index level (FRED NASDAQCOM); daily, in index points.

crossasset/dgs2.title: 2-year Treasury yield
crossasset/dgs2.why: The policy-expectations yield. Its 21-session change separates a market fall the Fed is expected to answer from one it is expected to watch.
crossasset/dgs2.definition: 2-year Treasury constant maturity rate (FRED DGS2); daily, in percent.

crossasset/dgs10.title: 10-year Treasury yield
crossasset/dgs10.why: The long rate. A 21-session move of 40 bp or more, either way, is the rates-shock fingerprint — the direction decides whether it is a growth scare or an inflation scare.
crossasset/dgs10.definition: 10-year Treasury constant maturity rate (FRED DGS10); daily, in percent.

crossasset/t10yie.title: 10-year breakeven inflation
crossasset/t10yie.why: The market's 10-year inflation expectation, priced daily: separates an inflation scare the market believes from one it expects policy to crush.
crossasset/t10yie.definition: 10-year breakeven inflation rate (FRED T10YIE); daily, in percent.

crossasset/dfii10.title: 10-year real yield (TIPS)
crossasset/dfii10.why: The real long rate — the tightness of financial conditions that does not depend on inflation expectations. Rising real yields into an equity fall mark a policy-driven event.
crossasset/dfii10.definition: 10-year Treasury inflation-indexed constant maturity rate (FRED DFII10); daily, in percent.

crossasset/dollar.title: Broad dollar index
crossasset/dollar.why: A rising dollar tightens global financial conditions with a lag; dollar momentum turns have led risk turns in tightening cycles. The dollar-turn inflection (Section 4 of the methodology) is computed from this series. Publication lags the observation by several days.
crossasset/dollar.definition: Nominal broad US dollar index (FRED DTWEXBGS); daily, index (Jan 2006 = 100).
crossasset/dollar.note: Publication lag: the latest print is several business days old at any build.

crossasset/euro.title: Euro (USD per EUR)
crossasset/euro.why: The bilateral leg of the dollar read and the spot rate behind the pulse layer's cross-currency basis: a euro falling with the broad dollar rising confirms a dollar event rather than a euro event.
crossasset/euro.definition: US dollar to one euro exchange rate (FRED DEXUSEU); daily, in USD per EUR.

crossasset/wti.title: WTI crude
crossasset/wti.why: The energy-shock leg: a 21-session move of 15% or more, either direction, is a fingerprint — up is a supply shock, down is the shock unwinding or demand failing, and the two have opposite inflation implications. Publication lags by about a week.
crossasset/wti.definition: Crude oil price, West Texas Intermediate (FRED DCOILWTICO); daily, in USD per barrel.
crossasset/wti.note: Publication lag: the latest print is about a week old at any build.

crossasset/brent.title: Brent crude
crossasset/brent.why: The global crude benchmark, beside WTI: the Brent–WTI gap separates a global supply event from a US logistics event.
crossasset/brent.definition: Crude oil price, Brent Europe (FRED DCOILBRENTEU); daily, in USD per barrel.
crossasset/brent.note: Publication lag: the latest print is about a week old at any build.

crossasset/bitcoin.title: Bitcoin
crossasset/bitcoin.why: The most liquid 24/7 risk asset: it trades through weekends and holidays when nothing else on the page does, so its weekend moves are the first print of the next session's risk appetite.
crossasset/bitcoin.definition: Coinbase Bitcoin price (FRED CBBTCUSD); daily, in USD.

crossasset/hyg.title: High-yield bonds (HYG)
crossasset/hyg.why: The traded price of high-yield credit — the equity market's own credit gauge, beside the OAS. Price and spread disagreeing is a flow signal, not a data error.
crossasset/hyg.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: HYG — finance.yahoo.com/quote/HYG
crossasset/hyg.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: HYG (unadjusted close)
crossasset/hyg.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYG), in USD; trading days only.

crossasset/lqd.title: Investment-grade bonds (LQD)
crossasset/lqd.why: The traded price of investment-grade credit — see HYG.
crossasset/lqd.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: LQD — finance.yahoo.com/quote/LQD
crossasset/lqd.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: LQD (unadjusted close)
crossasset/lqd.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF (LQD), in USD; trading days only.

crossasset/tlt.title: Long Treasuries (TLT)
crossasset/tlt.why: Duration as an asset: when equities fall and TLT rises, duration is doing the haven work; when both fall, the shock is in rates themselves.
crossasset/tlt.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: TLT — finance.yahoo.com/quote/TLT
crossasset/tlt.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: TLT (unadjusted close)
crossasset/tlt.definition: Daily unadjusted close of iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), in USD; trading days only.

crossasset/gld.title: Gold (GLD)
crossasset/gld.why: Gold. FRED's spot fixing series were retired by their source, so the free route is the ETF. The haven-bid fingerprint needs gold *up* while equities fall — gold falling with equities is reported as a failed haven, which is itself the signal.
crossasset/gld.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: GLD — finance.yahoo.com/quote/GLD
crossasset/gld.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: GLD (unadjusted close)
crossasset/gld.definition: Daily unadjusted close of SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), in USD; trading days only.
crossasset/gld.note: FRED retired both LBMA fixing series (GOLDAMGBD228NLBM / GOLDPMGBD228NLBM); the ETF is the free source.

crossasset/uso.title: Oil fund (USO)
crossasset/uso.why: The traded oil price, beside the FRED spot prints: USO trades daily with no publication lag, so it is the freshest energy read on the page (futures-based, so it carries roll yield).
crossasset/uso.source: Yahoo Finance chart API: USO — finance.yahoo.com/quote/USO
crossasset/uso.series_id: Yahoo Finance chart API: USO (unadjusted close)
crossasset/uso.definition: Daily unadjusted close of United States Oil Fund (USO), in USD; trading days only.

derived/vix_spread.title: Volatility term structure (VIX − VXV)
derived/vix_spread.why: Spot vol above 3-month vol (backwardation) is a coincident-to-slightly-leading stress marker: it flips at the onset of dislocations, and its normalisation has historically been one of the earliest signs a dislocation is ending. This spread is the vol-inversion fingerprint and the vol-curve-flip inflection.
derived/vix_spread.source: Computed by this build from FRED VIXCLS and VXVCLS, archived in this section — github.com/fcela/frb-heat-index (data/momentum)
derived/vix_spread.definition: CBOE Volatility Index minus CBOE VIX 3-Month Volatility Index, on dates both are observed (FRED VIXCLS, VXVCLS); daily, in vol points. Positive = backwardation (inversion).

derived/def_cyc_spread.title: Defensive-minus-cyclical momentum spread
derived/def_cyc_spread.why: The measured value behind the risk-off / risk-on rotation fingerprint, as a line: the 21-session return of the defensive trio (staples, utilities, health care) minus the cyclical trio (discretionary, industrials, technology). Sustained readings beyond ±3 pp are a rotation regime, not a day of noise.
derived/def_cyc_spread.source: Computed by this build from the archived sector closes in this section — github.com/fcela/frb-heat-index (data/momentum)
derived/def_cyc_spread.definition: Mean trailing 21-session return of XLP, XLU, XLV minus mean trailing 21-session return of XLY, XLI, XLK, on their common trading days; daily, in percentage points.
